verdict.cause: Two 2026 guidance cuts: FY26 sales now -5% to -7%, Americas comps -12% in Q2, underlying margins falling; brand losing US share
verdict.summary: Lululemon's slide comes from a shrinking core US business: Q2 Americas comparable sales fell 12%, total comps fell 9%, full-year revenue is guided down 5-7% and Q3 down 10-11%, and gross and operating margins excluding a one-off $134.5M tariff refund were roughly 360 and 750 basis points lower than a year ago. Management itself calls it a brand trust problem, on top of competition (Alo, Vuori) and tariffs, after three years of decline, so this looks like a competitive erosion of the brand rather than a passing dip, although a new CEO (Heidi O'Neill, since September) could still turn it. Watch Q3 results in December, US comparable sales and whether ex-refund margins stabilise.

verdict.summary: Fiserv cut 2026 adjusted EPS guidance to $7.20-7.40 from $8.00-8.30 with organic revenue now -1% to 0%, lost its second short-tenure CEO in June (Mike Lyons to Truist), and Q3 showed adjusted operating margin down to 31.2% from 37.0% plus a $6.45B goodwill impairment; the peer group fell about as much, so part of the slide is sector-wide. Whether the margin compression and impairment mark a permanently smaller business or a reset before recovery is not settled; watch Q4 return to revenue growth, merchant margins and 2027 guidance. Note: the model notes still quote the old $8.00-8.30 2026 guidance.
